decisions.reason: The necessary LED power-control effect is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY at message 281.
Shutting down the separate 5V rail does not change the standalone USB-powered 3.3V rail, its loads, or its source-selection behavior.
The source changes software control of the downstream 5V rail but does not change the AXP2101 selection, battery power path, or required system rails.
The source concerns shutdown of the 5V boost rail and does not alter DCDC1's 3.3V output voltage, current rating, or normal-operation role.
Controlling the 5V rail when LEDs are unnecessary does not necessarily change any ESP32 sleep mode, entry condition, wake source, or wake interval.
The 5V rail shutdown behavior does not affect the battery connector's family, pin count, pin functions, accessibility, or unresolved pin order.
The source does not change battery overcharge, overdischarge, thermal sensing, or thermal protection requirements.
The conditional shutdown of LED power when LEDs are unnecessary does not change the required charge-status indication path, connector, resistor, or population choices.
The source explains use of the existing 5V_EN signal but does not change its connector pin assignment or any other interboard signal-interface attribute.
GPIO3 was already assigned to 5V enable; the source adds rail-control behavior without changing the GPIO mapping.
The electrical shutdown behavior has no necessary effect on board dimensions, orientation, mounting, connector placement, or mechanical clearance.
The source does not change the interboard power connector, its pin count, or the rule that connector pin orders must match.
